title: Believing Scripture unto salvation needs the Spirit's inward impulse beyond argument
source_text: II. Probavimus, ad hoc ut aliquis Scripturae sacrae credat, illamque divinitus inspiratam agnoscat, vera et legitima fide quae sit alicujus ad salutem momenti, opus esse Spiritu sancto intus monente et illuminante. Illam autem Spiritus sancti operationem necessariam nobis esse, non tantum propter tenebras per peccatum inductas, quae sunt veluti quoddam velum, mentis nostrae oculis oppositum, quod occultat nobis Scripturae sacrae lucem, et obstat ne illam possimus aspicere; sed etiam propter genium et naturam ipsius doctrinae in Scriptura contentae: quae, cum mentem nostram in se, etiam citra peccatum consideratam, omnino superet, necesse est ut intellectus noster supra seipsum extollatur, ut ad illam possit assurgere. Adeoque, ut Scripturam et singulos ejus libros pro veris et divinis agnoscamus et recipiamus firmiter et indubitate, et certitudine tanta quantam requirit fides, ad cujus objectum pertinent, opus esse non solum ut Spiritus sanctus, mentis nostrae nativam caecitatem sanet, et dispellat tenebras per peccatum accersitas, quae obstant ne Scripturae lucem possimus percipere; sed etiam ut nos ad credendum compellat arcano quodam instinctu et impulsu, sive interna quadam efficacia, quae sit omni argumento et ratione major.
pass_a_gloss: We have proved that for someone to believe sacred Scripture, and to acknowledge it as divinely inspired, with a true and legitimate faith that is of any moment for salvation, there is need of the Holy Spirit inwardly admonishing and illuminating. And that that operation of the Holy Spirit is necessary for us, not only because of the darkness induced by sin, which is like a certain veil set opposite the eyes of our mind, which hides from us the light of sacred Scripture and prevents us from being able to look upon it; but also because of the character and nature of the doctrine itself contained in Scripture: which, since it altogether surpasses our mind in itself, even considered apart from sin, it is necessary that our intellect be raised above itself, so that it can rise to it. And therefore, that we may acknowledge and receive Scripture and its several books as true and divine firmly and without doubt, and with so great a certainty as faith requires — to whose object they belong — there is need not only that the Holy Spirit heal the native blindness of our mind and dispel the darkness brought on by sin, which hinder us from being able to perceive Scripture's light; but also that he compel us to believe by a certain secret instinct and impulse, or by a certain inward efficacy, which is greater than every argument and reason.
pass_b_english: We have proved this: to believe sacred Scripture, and to acknowledge it as divinely inspired, with a true and legitimate faith that matters for salvation, a person needs the Holy Spirit admonishing and illuminating within.

That work of the Spirit is necessary for us not only because of the darkness sin brings — a kind of veil set before the mind's eyes, hiding Scripture's light and keeping us from looking at it — but also because of the character and nature of the doctrine Scripture itself contains. That doctrine altogether surpasses our mind, even considered apart from sin. So our intellect must be lifted above itself if it is to rise to it.

Therefore, to acknowledge and receive Scripture and each of its books as true and divine — firmly, without doubt, and with the certainty faith requires, since they belong to faith's object — we need more than the Spirit healing our native blindness and driving off the darkness sin has fetched in, which blocks perception of Scripture's light. He must also compel us to believe by a secret instinct and impulse, or by an inward efficacy greater than every argument and reason.

lemmas.gloss: by a secret instinct and impulse

choices.why: Genius of the doctrine = its distinctive cast, not a personified spirit.
Keeps the strong verb; matches Pars II impulse language.
